clue.text: Cruel, cruel habit and endlessly revolting

indicators.note: something revolting is in revolt, turned over, so these letters are overturned into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

indicators.note: endlessly says the word and loses its final letter

explanation.surface: A complaint about someone's cruel and disgusting habit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endlessly' cuts AND to AN; 'revolting' then shuffles CRUEL, HABIT and AN together.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonyms: a cruel remark or person is unkind and lacking in charity.

clue.text: Take off and run past flashing

indicators.note: flashing suggests quick, darting movement, so the words run and past are thrown into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A streaker strips off and runs past, exposing themselves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flashing' looks like part of a streaking scene but tells you to rearrange RUN PAST.
explanation.definitionFit: To take off a harness or strap fastening is to release its buckle.

clue.text: Managed PC editor

parts.note: a PC (police constable) is a cop

explanation.surface: Someone ran a personal computer as its editor.
explanation.walkthrough: PC looks like a personal computer; here it is a police constable.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonyms: if you managed a hard situation, you got by or handled it.

clue.text: Enter game after resolving contract

indicators.note: resolving can mean breaking something into its parts and reforming it, so the letters of enter game are reworked

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Instructions to join a game once a contract is settled.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonyms: a contract is a formal agreement between parties.

clue.text: It's one tiny amount initially

indicators.note: initially points to the first letter of each of the four words before it

explanation.surface: A description of a tiny quantity, the very beginning of something.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines the answer while its initials spell it.
explanation.definitionFit: The Greek letter's name is used idiomatically for the smallest possible amount, as in 'not one jot'.

clue.text: Sailor in charge, in time, quit

parts.note: AB, able-bodied seaman, is a common crossword sailor

indicators.note: the second in says the abbreviation for in charge sits inside the word for time

parts.note: a date is a point in time
in charge is abbreviated IC, as in second-in-command or 2IC

explanation.surface: A sailor who was in charge left his post at the right moment.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads 'in time' as 'promptly'; 'time' alone is a date and the comma-split 'in' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: To abdicate is to give up a throne or duty, i.e. to resign or step down.

clue.text: Constitutional member, a Labour leader

parts.note: a limb such as a leg is a member of the body

indicators.note: leader indicates the opening letter of Labour

explanation.surface: A Labour leader who is a member of a constitutional body.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Labour leader' reads as a party chief; here it is just L.
explanation.definitionFit: Something constitutional is permitted by the constitution, so lawful.

clue.text: Willing to take motorway home

indicators.note: to take says the first word holds the motorway inside it

parts.note: docile means compliant, willing to obey
the M1 is Britain's main north-south motorway, written MI in crosswords

explanation.surface: Someone happy to drive the motorway home.
explanation.walkthrough: The M1 is a British motorway from London to Leeds; its name doubles as letters MI.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonyms: a domicile is the place where one lives, a dwelling.

clue.text: Scheming to trap fool with satisfaction

indicators.note: to trap says the first word encloses the second

parts.note: sly means cunning or scheming
a mug is a gullible person, a fool

explanation.surface: A con artist schemes to trap a fool and is pleased with it.
explanation.definitionFit: Self-satisfied manner: acting smugly is acting with complacent satisfaction.

clue.text: Settled admitting father right to get divorced

indicators.note: admitting means letting in, so the first word holds the others

parts.note: seated means settled in a chair
pa is an informal word for father

explanation.surface: A settlement that let father get a divorce.
explanation.definitionFit: Divorced couples have parted; the adjective means living apart, split.

clue.text: Spruce up grand space

parts.note: G is the abbreviation for grand, a thousand
room means space, as in room to move

explanation.surface: An invitation to tidy up a large space.
explanation.definitionFit: To groom is to tidy one's appearance, smartening oneself.

clue.text: Controlled animal's lair after purge

indicators.note: after says the lair comes after the purge in the answer

parts.note: to rid a place of something is to purge it
a den is a wild animal's lair

explanation.surface: A cleared-out animal den taken over after a purge.
explanation.definitionFit: Participle sense: a horse that is ridden is steered and kept in check by its rider.

clue.text: Telling-off, catching chill in grass

indicators.note: catching means holding, so the first word encloses the second

parts.note: to grass is to inform on someone, also to sing to the police
a chill is a cold

explanation.surface: Being told off for catching a chill while lying on the grass.
explanation.walkthrough: 'grass' looks like lawn; it is the slang verb for informing, as is 'sing'.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonyms: a scolding is a reprimand or rebuke.

clue.text: Comparatively confined in dock, accepting fine

indicators.note: accepting means taking in, so the first word holds the second

parts.note: a pier is a landing stage where boats dock
OK means fine, all right

explanation.surface: A cramped dock that is acceptable for its purpose.
explanation.definitionFit: Poky means small and cramped, so the comparative means more cramped.

clue.text: Affection of family head ringing daughter

indicators.note: ringing means surrounding, so the family and head pieces encircle the daughter

parts.note: kin are one's family
a ness is a headland

explanation.surface: The head of a family calls their daughter out of fondness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'head' is a headland, NESS, not a chief.
explanation.definitionFit: Kindness is warm, caring regard for others, closely akin to fondness.

clue.text: It delays getting drunk with regularity

indicators.note: getting drunk suggests staggering about, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Getting drunk regularly holds things up.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something at a steady, even rate means doing it with regularity.

clue.text: Some peculiar gent in Asian republic

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: An odd man in Asia who is from a different country.
explanation.definitionFit: The South American country is a federal republic with an elected president.

clue.text: Forward found in girl's bed

parts.note: Di is a girl's name, and 's gives the S of the possessive
a flower bed is a patch of ground

explanation.surface: Something found in a girl's bed being sent on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Forward' is a verb, to send on.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonyms: to dispatch a letter or parcel is to send it on its way.

clue.text: Intense scheming consuming the compiler's genius!

indicators.note: consuming means swallowing, so the rearranged letters take in the compiler
scheming suggests plotting and rearranging, so the letters of intense are reordered

parts.note: taken as written
the compiler refers to themselves, I

explanation.surface: An exclamation praising a brilliant compiler's intense plotting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'scheming' turns INTENSE into EINSTEN, and 'consuming' puts I inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: The physicist's surname is used as a byword for any exceptional mind.

clue.text: Former capital of Portugal

parts.note: capital here is money, not a city: the currency Portugal used before the euro

explanation.surface: A trivia question about Portugal's old seat of government.
explanation.walkthrough: 'capital' tempts a city answer such as Coimbra; it is money.
explanation.definitionFit: Portugal's currency until the euro arrived in 2002; capital means funds.

clue.text: Shining silver pound sweetheart's pocketed

parts.note: Ag is the chemical symbol for silver

indicators.note: pocketed means placed inside, so the sweetheart goes within the pound piece

parts.note: to lam is to beat or pound
the heart of the word sweet is its middle letter, E

explanation.surface: A silver pound coin kept in a lover's pocket.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pound' is the verb to strike, LAM, not money; 'sweetheart' is the centre of SWEET.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonyms: something gleaming or glowing with light is shining.

clue.text: Musical portion's over, captured by microphone

indicators.note: captured by says the reversed portion sits inside the microphone

parts.note: mic is short for microphone

indicators.note: over means turned over, so the word for portion is read backwards

parts.note: a dole is a share or portion handed out

explanation.surface: A tuneful section has ended, recorded on a microphone.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonyms: melodic means tuneful, pleasing to the ear.

clue.text: Inside place, not a pharaoh's empty tomb

indicators.note: Inside says the answer sits within the following words, across their breaks

explanation.surface: An empty tomb that isn't a pharaoh's.
explanation.walkthrough: The pharaoh pushes towards Egyptian tombs; the answer is a war memorial.
explanation.definitionFit: A cenotaph is a monument to people buried elsewhere, literally Greek for empty tomb.

clue.text: Gashed gripping hard point

indicators.note: gripping means holding fast, so the first word encloses the letter

parts.note: torn means ripped or gashed
H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils

explanation.surface: A wound gashed by a hard point.
explanation.definitionFit: A thorn is a sharp spike on a plant stem.

clue.text: Bird's back with practically complete beast

indicators.note: back says the bird's name is read in reverse

parts.note: the mina, or myna, is an Asian starling

indicators.note: practically means nearly, so the word for complete loses its last letter

parts.note: all means complete, whole

explanation.surface: A bird returns with the creature nearly complete.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns MINA to ANIM; 'practically' cuts ALL to AL.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonyms: a beast is any creature, especially a large one.

clue.text: The bulk keeps one clammy

indicators.note: keeps means holds, so the first piece contains the second

parts.note: the bulk of something is most of it
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Most of something stays damp and clammy.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonyms: clammy means unpleasantly damp.

clue.text: Reportedly makes vases

indicators.note: Reportedly says the word is heard rather than read

parts.note: to make money is to earn it

explanation.surface: A rumour that someone produces vases.
explanation.walkthrough: In a non-rhotic British accent the two words sound the same.
explanation.definitionFit: Urns are tall rounded vessels, ornamental vases.

clue.text: Detectives seen with company in nightclub

parts.note: DIs are detective inspectors

explanation.surface: Police seen with friends in a nightclub.
explanation.definitionFit: A disco is a club for dancing to recorded music.

clue.text: Scared by blunder provided, held by United

indicators.note: held by means contained within, so the blunder and proviso go inside the word for united

parts.note: tied means bound together, united
to err is to make a mistake
if means provided that

explanation.surface: A footballer scared by a blunder that United made.
explanation.walkthrough: United looks like the football club; here it means joined.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonyms: someone terrified is extremely frightened.

clue.text: Sauciest hint changed, becoming zealous

indicators.note: changed means altered, so the letters of the two words are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A cheeky suggestion altered to sound more eager.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonyms: zealous means eager and keen.
